name: inventory
about: Pilot project session: a tiny Python stock list (library + CLI). 10 owner requests: some independent, some depending on earlier ones, several sharing inv/store.py, inv/cli.py or inv/report.py, one vague request (R08) and one change of mind (R09).

settle.message: Status check from the owner: is everything I asked for finished and merged? Reply DONE if so.

symcc: Set the test command to `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` and use auto mode.

requests.text: Items need a price. Let `Inventory.add(name, qty=1, price=None)` take an optional unit price (a float; the last price given for an item wins, items with no price count as 0), add `Inventory.price(name)` and `Inventory.total_value()` which is the sum of qty x price over all items.

Removing more than we have makes the count go negative. `remove` should raise ValueError in that case and leave the count as it was. Removing the last one should take the item off the list completely.
Add `Inventory.save(path)` and a classmethod `Inventory.load(path)` that write and read the stock list as JSON. Prices must survive a save and load too.
The `list` command should print items sorted by name, one per line as `name: qty`.
Add a `value` command to the CLI that prints the total stock value with two decimals, like `total: 12.50`. The `add` command should take the price as an option: `add pen 3 --price 1.5`.
Item names should not care about upper or lower case: `Apple` and `apple` are the same item. Keep the name as it was first added for display.
New module `inv/report.py` with `low_stock(inv, threshold=5)`: the names of items with fewer than `threshold` in stock, sorted by name.
The CLI forgets everything between runs. Make it remember.
Change of mind on the list output: show the price too, as `name: qty @ price` with the price to two decimals (e.g. `pen: 3 @ 1.50`). Keep it sorted by name.
Add `csv_export(inv)` to `inv/report.py`: returns CSV text with the header `name,qty,price` and one row per item, sorted by name.

answers.answer: Add a `--file PATH` option to the CLI (before the command, e.g. `inv --file stock.json add pen 2`), default `inventory.json` in the current folder. Load it at the start if it exists and save it after `add` and `remove`. `main(argv)` with no `inv` given should use that file.
Prices print with two decimals; an item with no price shows 0.00.
Match names case-insensitively; show the spelling used the first time the item was added.

default_answer: Decide yourself, do what you think is best.
